second_order: making, moving and preserving the seolheart
theme_note: These passages do the practical work of calling people in, choosing coordinates and a design, moving after defeat, supplying a visual guide, and shifting from expansion to preservation. What varies is the stage of the same heart-making practice: recruitment, relocation, design, rebuilding, and upkeep.
regrouped_from: Reviewed against a provisional broader 'working on the canvas' group; kept this narrower and moved conflict, celebration, and negotiation into their own themes because they are different practices, not merely different words.

second_order: calling for power when other groups draw over the heart
theme_note: Each passage rallies more people to resist another group drawing over or overrunning the heart. The named opponents and intensity vary, from mourning an overrun to calling for a fight back.
regrouped_from: Reviewed beside the Jets argument; kept apart because these passages recruit defenders, while the Jets exchange disputes ownership and how the win happened.

second_order: arguing over wiping out and stealing the Jets logo
theme_note: The exchange works out what happened to the Jets area and who deserves blame or credit, then includes an offer to help after relocation. It varies between questions about scripts, joking claims of friendship or Seol power, accusations of theft and meanness, and attempted repair.
regrouped_from: Reviewed as a possible part of defending the heart, then separated because both insiders and an outsider are accounting for a wiped-out Jets logo rather than rallying defense of the heart.

second_order: celebrating the heart and rewarding the effort
theme_note: These passages mark success, thank contributors, praise the finished work, and turn the room's ordinary rare-Seol picture sharing into a reward. The celebration ranges from pride and affection to a promised image release and an outsider's praise.
regrouped_from: Reviewed after provisional grouping; no regrouping. Kept the rare-picture reward here because its function in this thread is thanking pixel work, even though image sharing predates the event.

second_order: working out how Korea can fit around the heart
theme_note: Across one negotiation, participants ask permission, admit erasing, report disagreement inside the group, invoke prior permission, propose compromises, and spread plans so writing can fit without overlapping the heart. What varies is both position and authority: there is no single settled community voice at first.
regrouped_from: Reviewed against a generic 'helping neighbors' group and regrouped into its own theme because these turns negotiate a contested shared boundary; the small-logo turns merely request help and receive resistance.

second_order: asking for help with nearby small logos
theme_note: Visitors use the thread to request help for Crystal Clear and WJSN projects near other K-pop marks. What varies is the response: one request simply stands, while the WJSN proposal reports relocation and meets a hostile refusal.
regrouped_from: Regrouped from an early 'negotiating with visitors' group: unlike the Korea exchange, these codes do not jointly bargain over this group's heart and therefore remain a distinct request-and-response practice.

second_order: updating models and scripts so work sticks
theme_note: The two passages diagnose people undoing work with outdated designs and tell script users exactly what changed. One explains the repeated damage; the other gives revised pixel instructions.
regrouped_from: Reviewed as a possible part of preserving the heart, then separated because the practice is synchronizing models and scripts rather than placing or defending pixels itself.
